feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: Cloaked in anonymity, Israeli soldiers describe mass civilian killings in 'NAZA'
entry.summary: NAZA is an acronym for nezek agavi, Hebrew for "collateral damage." It refers to the number of civilian casualties the Israeli military deems acceptable. The documentary is made by Israeli filmmakers.

entry.title: Cornell rape case gets special prosecutor. And, Renee Good's family sues the government
entry.summary: New legal action in two closely watched cases: one at Cornell, the other over Renee Good's death. We take a closer look.

entry.title: Pro-democracy activists increasingly vulnerable to authoritarian governments in Southeast Asia
entry.summary: Activists across Asia are being hunted down by authoritarian governments even across international borders. Human rights groups have been warning of a "swap market" of repression in Southeast Asia.

entry.title: What a Pearly King taught me about Cockney rhyming slang and East London history
entry.summary: In mother-of-pearl suits, the Pearly Kings used to canvass East London for charity. The most famous one, George Major, died in August. A look back on this larger-than-life figure and the Pearly King tradition.

entry.title: Passengers recount chaos on Tel Aviv flight. And, FBI probes employee-data hack
entry.summary: What we know so far about the tense moments aboard a Tel Aviv-bound flight. And, the FBI investigates a cyberattack involving sensitive employee data.

entry.title: Israel's prime minister says a pilot tried to crash a plane traveling to Tel Aviv
entry.summary: One pilot stabbed another pilot on a FlyDubai flight headed to Tel Aviv on Wednesday and may have tried to crash the plane before passengers and crew members subdued him, Israel's prime minister says.

entry.title: Picanha, prices and politics: What Brazil's favorite steak says about the election
entry.summary: President Lula promised Brazilians four years ago they'd be able to afford picanha again. Now, as he seeks another term, the price of the country's favorite cut of beef is telling a different story.

entry.title: What life under U.S. sanctions looks like for one ICC judge
entry.summary: Kimberly Prost, a Canadian judge at the International Criminal Court, says U.S. sanctions disrupted her daily life. She is still hearing cases and challenging the sanctions in court.

entry.title: Swiss glaciers suffer another year of record ice loss
entry.summary: Switzerland's glaciers are disappearing at a record pace. More than 5% of their ice has vanished this year alone — threatening water supplies, ecosystems and communities across Europe.

entry.title: Greetings from Syria, where time seems to melt as a glassmaker braves scorching temps
entry.summary: As a Syrian glassmaker created his wares in Damascus, watching his craft reminded this reporter to slow down and enjoy the moment.
